name: The Major and Minor Prophets (Latter Prophets): Judgment and Hope

objectives.text: Identify a prophet as a messenger whom God called to speak his words to his people
Retell the story of Jonah, including God's call, Jonah's flight, the great fish, and Nineveh's repentance
Recall that the prophets warned God's people to turn away from sin and return to the Lord
Retell the accounts of Daniel's friends in the furnace and Daniel in the lions' den and describe how God kept them faithful and safe
Identify promises in the prophets about a coming King and Savior and match them to their fulfillment in Jesus
Summarize the prophets' twofold message as a warning of judgment for sin and a promise of comfort and restoration
List the books of the Major and Minor Prophets in their order in the English Bible
Explain that the labels Major and Minor Prophets describe the length of the books rather than their importance
Compare Isaiah's response to his call with Jonah's flight from his call
Describe the main sins the prophets condemned, including idolatry, injustice toward the poor, and empty religious ritual
Classify the prophets as preexilic, exilic, or postexilic and describe the Assyrian, Babylonian, and Persian setting of each group
Explain how Jonah and Isaiah reveal God's purpose to show mercy to the nations beyond Israel
Explain how Malachi closes the Old Testament with the promise of a messenger that the New Testament fulfills in John the Baptist
Analyze the theme of the Day of the Lord as both judgment on the wicked and deliverance for God's people across several prophets
Explain how the prophets acted as messengers of the covenant who brought God's charges against his people based on the covenant's blessings and curses
Interpret the new covenant promises in Jeremiah and Ezekiel and explain how the book of Hebrews applies them to Christ
Explain how the Suffering Servant passage describes substitutionary suffering and how the New Testament identifies the Servant as Jesus
Analyze the literary forms of prophetic speech, including the messenger formula, judgment oracle, woe oracle, salvation oracle, and symbolic action
Construct a timeline that places each prophet alongside the kings and empires of his day using the superscriptions of the books
Apply the principle that the prophets testified beforehand to Christ when interpreting a prophetic passage
Analyze the symbolism of apocalyptic visions in Daniel and Zechariah and explain sound principles for interpreting them
Analyze Hosea's marriage imagery as a portrayal of Israel's covenant unfaithfulness and God's steadfast love
Evaluate how the prophets' call for justice and mercy informs Christian responsibility toward neighbors today
Defend the Reformed view that predictive prophecy displays God's sovereign knowledge and decree in response to critical claims about the dating of Isaiah and Daniel
Create a thematic synthesis tracing how judgment in the Latter Prophets serves God's purpose of preserving a remnant and leads to the hope of restoration and new creation

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (prophet as messenger, call to repentance, messianic promises, judgment and hope summary, Major and Minor distinction, Isaiah and Jonah comparison, Daniel, Day of the Lord, new covenant, Suffering Servant, covenant lawsuit, timeline, Hosea, predictive prophecy, final synthesis). Dropped the bare naming objective in favor of retelling Jonah and listing the books in order. Added objectives on sins the prophets condemned, historical periods of the prophets, mercy to the nations, Malachi as bridge to John the Baptist, prophetic literary forms, Christ-centered reading, apocalyptic interpretation, and prophetic justice. Replaced vague verbs (observe, connect) with assessable ones, added verse anchors throughout, and attached confessions only where they state the doctrine, correcting citations to Westminster Confession of Faith format and adding WCF 7.5, 7.6, 1.5, 3.1 and WSC Q25.
